title: Initialization writes the marked blank block
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine with $k$ work tapes over a finite alphabet. For any input word $x$, input-head position $p$, integer frontier $z$, output word $o$, and two lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols of the simulator alphabet, start the simulator in the initialization state with counter $0$ in the zipper configuration determined by these data. After exactly $k$ steps, it is in the initialization state with counter $k$, frontier $z+k$, left stack equal to the reverse of the encoded marked blank block followed by $l$, and right stack equal to $r$ with its first $k$ entries removed; the input-head position and output word are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has a finite state set and decidable state equality
$x$ is an input word over the simulator alphabet
$l$ and $r$ are finite lists of possibly blank simulator symbols
replaced:
For the single-tape simulator of a machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes: from any
forward-facing zipper configuration whose control is in the initialization phase with
counter $0$, running exactly $k$ transitions writes, one cell per step while moving
right, the encoded marked blank block over the next $k$ cells, ending in the
initialization phase with counter $k$ and with the work head advanced by $k$ cells; the
input head, output, and remaining tape contents are unchanged.
